Chapter 7: Healing and Moving Forward—Rebuilding Trust and Self-Compassion.
Let’s talk about what comes next, especially if you’ve ever found yourself in the sidepiece role. Healing really is the next big step, isn’t it? The emotional aftermath can be tough—you might feel betrayed, ashamed, or even start doubting yourself.
Rebuilding trust, both in yourself and in others, takes time. It’s all about patience, self-compassion, and making some intentional choices along the way.
Healing usually begins with something simple, but powerful: just letting yourself admit the pain and grieve a little. It’s totally normal to feel anger, sadness, or regret. If you try to push those feelings away, it only stretches out the healing process. Instead, give yourself permission to be honest about how you feel, and let those emotions move through you.
So, what really helps with healing? There are a few key things to focus on:
First, practice self-forgiveness. Remember, everybody makes mistakes. The fact that you were in this position doesn’t define who you are or what your future can look like.
Next, think about reaching out for professional support. Whether it’s a therapist or a counselor, talking to someone trained to help can give you a safe space to process everything, challenge those tough beliefs about yourself, and help you build healthier relationships down the road.
Reconnecting with your own values is huge, too. What really matters to you? Maybe it’s honesty, respect, or being open with others. When you reflect on these things, they can guide your next steps and help you feel a sense of integrity again.
And don’t forget about the people who make you feel good—family, friends, your community. Investing in those connections can remind you of your worth, and help rebuild trust in a safe, supportive way. Sometimes, just spending time with people who truly care about you is the best medicine.
There are plenty of real-life stories out there showing that healing is absolutely possible. Someone who chooses to take time for reflection, who seeks support and sets new boundaries, can actually come out the other side feeling more confident and self-assured. And when you forgive yourself and let go of the shame, you open the door to moving forward with more clarity and confidence than before.
Healing isn’t a straight line. There’ll be ups and downs, and moments when you wonder if you’re making any progress at all. But here’s what matters—if you give yourself patience and a dose of self-kindness, you can come out of this with a deeper understanding of who you are, and a renewed commitment to building healthy, honest relationships in the future.
